detect-names-and-quotes-no-score:
This reads as strongly machine-made. Almost every clause is a tell, and there's no fact underneath any of them to preserve.

- "In today's fast-paced digital landscape" — throat-clearing opener (A4), stacked with dead inflation language (B8: *landscape*).
- "isn't just a tool - it's a partner" — not-X-but-Y staging (A1), plus a spaced dash used as an em dash (C5).
- "It stands as a testament to" — avoids the plain verb (B7) and borrows false significance (B1: *testament to*).
- "pivotal commitment" — inflated significance with no checkable claim behind it (B1/B8).
- "seamless, vibrant collaboration" — two AI-vocabulary adjectives stacked on one noun (B8: *seamless*, *vibrant*).
- "empowering teams to unlock their full potential" — vague declarative with nothing specific in it (B2); *empower* and *unlock potential* are both stock AI phrasing.

What's missing is as telling as what's there: no product, no feature, no user, no outcome — nothing a reader could act on or check. Nothing here reads as a person; there's no specific detail, no uneven rhythm, no stance beyond generic enthusiasm.

Dear Orla,

My name is Dan, and I run ScentVerdict, a fragrance review site I started last year after getting frustrated with how hard it was to find honest reviews of niche perfumes.

Every review is based on at least two weeks of wear, and we score longevity, projection and value separately, because a single star rating hides too much. Over the last twelve months we have published 2,400 reviews, and our readers tell us the separate scores are the reason they come back.

I have been following your house for a while, and I think your approach to small-batch releases is exactly the kind of story our readers care about. I would love to review your autumn collection, and I am happy to share our methodology in more detail: how we handle samples, how we disclose free products, and how we keep the review independent of any commercial relationship.

We also run a monthly newsletter for our most engaged readers, and have a small but growing presence on Instagram and TikTok, where short wear-test videos have done particularly well.

Do get in touch if this sounds interesting. I would be glad to set up a call at a time that suits you.

Kind regards,
Dan

First contact (not cut): 205 words. Paragraph 4, on the newsletter and social channels, is the detail a link could carry.
